Bounded findings:

- **Cursor reuse works.** `clear()` sets position to zero, limit to capacity, and discards the view’s mark without erasing content. This removes the previous record’s restrictive limit before `position(begin)`. After `limit(end)`, digest update consumes precisely `[begin,end)` and, on normal return, leaves position equal to end and limit unchanged. Empty windows are valid; the default SPI returns immediately.
- **Bounds validation remains essential.** Preserve `0 ≤ begin ≤ end ≤ validated image bound ≤ capacity`, with overflow checked before conversion to integer indices. `clear()` exposes capacity beyond any prior logical limit. Moreover, `limit(end)` silently clamps position when `end < begin`; the sequence itself does **not** reject reversed windows. These behaviors follow directly from [Buffer’s setters](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/890adb6410dab4606a4f26a942aed02fb2f55387/src/java.base/share/classes/java/nio/Buffer.java#L325-L385).
- **Nonzero position is preserved initially, not rebased.** `asReadOnlyBuffer()` initially copies capacity, position, limit and mark, then maintains independent cursor state. It does not make the current position index zero. Directory coordinates must match that view’s index space. Clearing or consuming the view leaves the original buffer’s position, limit and mark intact. Its initial byte order is big endian; bytewise digest input is unaffected. [ByteBuffer template](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/890adb6410dab4606a4f26a942aed02fb2f55387/src/java.base/share/classes/java/nio/X-Buffer.java.template#L660-L683).
- **Read-only does not establish a retention boundary.** Content remains shared. The public API forwards the actual buffer to the provider; an override can retain it and change its cursor/limit. Constructor-local scope therefore does not prove non-escape, and a limited view does not conceal other bytes within its capacity. **Never remove the existing copy protecting private `recordDigests`.** Preserve existing backing-storage lifetime and digest/finalization ordering. [Provider delegation](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/890adb6410dab4606a4f26a942aed02fb2f55387/src/java.base/share/classes/java/security/MessageDigest.java#L656-L659).
- **This removes repeated view creation, without proving zero allocation or zero copying.** Read-only heap buffers report `hasArray() == false`. The inherited SPI therefore copies through its retained, reusable temporary array, bounded to 4096 bytes in this revision; providers may override that route. [Array accessibility](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/890adb6410dab4606a4f26a942aed02fb2f55387/src/java.base/share/classes/java/nio/X-Buffer.java.template#L1469-L1482), [SPI fallback](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/890adb6410dab4606a4f26a942aed02fb2f55387/src/java.base/share/classes/java/security/MessageDigestSpi.java#L111-L134), [size bound](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/890adb6410dab4606a4f26a942aed02fb2f55387/src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security/jca/JCAUtil.java#L49-L60).

The constructor independently requires each `(offset,length)` to satisfy nonnegative values and `(long)offset + length <= units`. It does **not** require physical ordering, disjointness, adjacency, full payload coverage, or `sum(lengths) == units`. Dimensions, image checksum, strict logical ordering, and v2 Java hashes remain mandatory.

These are concrete source-derived valid layouts. Offsets and lengths are **UTF-16 units relative to the payload**:

| Case | Physical payload | Directory `(offset,length)` in logical order | Logical records |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backward, disjoint | `ba` | `(1,1), (0,1)` | `a`, `b` |
| Same-start containment | `ab` | `(0,1), (0,2)` | `a`, `ab` |
| Partial overlap | `abc` | `(0,2), (1,2)` | `ab`, `bc` |
| Containment with backward offset | `ba` | `(1,1), (0,2)` | `a`, `ba` |
| Empty at payload end | `a` | `(1,0), (0,1)` | empty, `a` |
| Unreferenced gap | `a?b` | `(0,1), (2,1)` | `a`, `b` |

An empty record may point anywhere from offset zero through `units`, inclusive. Strict ordering permits at most one, necessarily the first logical record. Repeated identical spans are rejected because their values duplicate; equal offsets with different lengths can be valid. Zero records with nonempty payload are also accepted.

The incumbent test builder concatenates records. Its successful fixtures therefore do not establish coverage for backward offsets, overlaps, gaps, or empty records positioned at payload end.
